title: dedicated-autoscaler: burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting optimizations
author: Priya Nair
release_notes:
- Improve autoscaler burst window smoothing to reduce oscillation under bursty arrival patterns.
- Add throughput guarantee policy and SLA metric emitters for Dedicated fleets.
- Extend utilization reporting with per-fleet and per-model 1m/5m/15m aggregates and export to Console.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets have reported occasional capacity thrash during short, high-concurrency bursts (support threads ENG-4821). This leads to transient throttling and missed throughput guarantees. We need a targeted set of changes to the autoscaler and reporting to: 1) provide predictable burst allowances without destabilizing steady-state scaling, 2) expose throughput-guarantee metrics so SRE and customers can reason about SLAs, and 3) improve utilization visibility to tune autoscaler policies.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduces a burst credit bucket and smoothing window in the dedicated autoscaler; credits are earned during underutilization and consumed during bursts. 2) Adds an optional throughput_guarantee policy that pins a minimum concurrent slots reservation per fleet and emits guarantee breach events. 3) Enhances utilization reporting: adds per-fleet 1m/5m/15m utilization aggregates, model-level hotness heatmap counters, and an exporter that feeds Redwood Console and the autoscaler's decision engine. 4) Performance/ops: minor optimizations in the scheduler loop and guarded KV-cache lookups to reduce contention under high request rates.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4821). - [x] Unit + integration tests for burst bucket logic. - [x] End-to-end smoke test against a local dedicated cluster. - [x] Observability: metrics, logs, and Console panel changes. - [x] Backwards-compatible defaults for fleets without policy set.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative for rollout: feature gated behind fleet.policy.v2 with default off. Early customers can opt-in. We will ship with a staged canary rollout and monitor the new metrics for two weeks before enabling by default.

review_conversation:
Alex Chen: requested more tests around clock skew and credit decay; noted edge case where two fleets share a single node pool.
Priya Nair: responded with explanation and added additional unit tests and an integration scenario for shared pools (see test_throughput_guarantee.py).
Samir Patel: requested metrics dimensionality limits to avoid high-cardinality explosion; we capped model hotness heatmap to top-50 models per fleet and added sampling.
Jordan Lee: verified performance impact on scheduler in a local perf run and approved after seeing <2% p99 latency regression.
Status: approved by Alex, Samir, Jordan. Author addressed requested changes and CI is green.
ci_checks: CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration smoke (pass), lint (pass), e2e-dedicated-canary (flaky -> rerun -> pass). Notable: initial e2e run failed due to test timing; fixed by adding a retry+idempotent cleanup in tests. Final run green.
observability_notes: New metrics: redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization.{1m,5m,15m} (gauge), redwood.dedicated.fleet.credit_balance (gauge), redwood.dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee.breach (counter), redwood.dedicated.model.hotness.topN (histogram/sample). Console panels added and dashboard JSON updated. Alerts: added SLO alert when throughput_guarantee.breach rate > 0.5% over 5m.
backwards_compat: Feature gated behind fleet.policy.v2. Default behavior unchanged for fleets without configuration. Policy schema changes are additive and validated at API ingress. Migration doc included in README.md.
testing_instructions: Unit tests included (pytest). Integration: run redwood-infra/local_dedicated.sh to bring up a small cluster, apply sample fleet policy in tests/fixtures, and run tests/integration/test_throughput_guarantee.py. Console panels available under 'Dedicated -> Fleet Guarantees' after deploying the dashboard JSON.
changelog_entry: Improve Dedicated autoscaler: burst credit smoothing, throughput guarantees, and richer utilization reporting (opt-in).
post_merge_actions: 1) Roll out feature flag to 5% of fleets for 48h and monitor 'credit_balance' and 'throughput_guarantee.breach' metrics. 2) If stable, expand to 50% and then 100% over two weeks. 3) Inform customer success for fleets with explicit SLA commitments.
notes: Conservative approach: metrics and policy validation added to allow safe rollback. No DB migrations were required. Live experiments will be gated via feature flag to avoid customer impact.
